title: Api
description:
Every JSON request and response body of the versioned HTTP API, in one place.

This file exists because of one fact: a native app cannot be force-updated. Once a build is in a store, old versions keep calling these routes for months, so an unannounced change to a body is an outage for someone who cannot install the fix. Bodies are therefore evolved ADDITIVELY inside a version, and a shape that genuinely cannot be evolved gets a new version prefix instead.

`ApiVersion`, `ClientConfig` and `UpgradeRequired` below are the negotiation itself — what a client sends, what the server answers, and how the server says 'you are too old to be safe'.

_unused.description: This document is a definitions container; the API has no single root body. Types come from `definitions`.

apiVersion.title: ApiVersion
apiVersion.description: The path segment every route lives under (`/api/v1/...`). Adding a member here is how a breaking change ships: the old version keeps answering for its whole support window while the new one is adopted.

apiError.title: ApiError
apiError.description: The one error envelope. A machine-readable `error` code plus a human `message` — clients switch on the code, and never on the prose, which is free to change.

upgradeRequired.title: UpgradeRequired
upgradeRequired.description:
The body of a 426. The escape hatch for the case where compatibility is genuinely impossible — it should be rare, and it must exist, because the alternative is a client that fails every request with no way to explain why.

A client that receives this must show a real screen, not a failed request.

minimumVersion.description: The oldest client build still served, as `major.minor.patch`.

currentVersion.description: The newest build the server knows about — what the store is expected to offer.

storeUrl.description: Where to go and update. Null when the platform is unknown, in which case the client falls back to its own store link.

clientConfig.title: ClientConfig
clientConfig.description: What a client asks for at launch, before it trusts anything else. Unauthenticated on purpose: a client too old to authenticate must still be able to learn that it is too old.

supportedApiVersions.description: Every version prefix still answering, newest last. A version leaves this list only after its published deprecation window closes.

deprecatedApiVersions.description: Still answering, but scheduled for removal. A client on one of these is told by the `Deprecation` and `Sunset` response headers as well.

minimumArtifactSchema.description: The oldest `analysis.json` schema_version a client must still be able to render. Stored artifacts are served AS WRITTEN — §38 forbids reprocessing that buys nothing — so this is the floor a renderer has to cope with, not a promise that everything is current.

currentArtifactSchema.description: The schema_version freshly analysed swings are written at.

sunsetOn.description: ISO-8601 date this version stops answering.

swingViewSummary.title: SwingViewSummary
swingViewSummary.description: One camera's recording of a swing, as the log and the player need it.

mediaKey.description: The analyzer's working-directory stem. NOT an address — storage keys are derived from identity, never stored.

revision.description: Which analysis run's artifacts this view currently addresses. A re-analysis writes r<n+1> and only then repoints the row, so a golfer mid-scrub finishes on what they started with.

id.description: The swing's own uuid. Since migration 0006 this is NOT a folder name.

label.description: What to call this swing on screen — a uuid is useless to a person, so the human-facing name is explicit.

referenceLabel.description: Set on the bundled model swings; null on a golfer's own.

status.description: Rolled up across views: `ready` only when every view is, `failed` if any failed.

model.description: Display-only extras below are still read from `analysis.json` rather than denormalized onto the swing row. Cheap at today's counts; promoting them to columns is an additive migration, not a rearchitecture.

headMarker.title: HeadMarker
headMarker.description: A hand-placed club head, normalized 0–1 against the video frame — the same convention as `analysis.json`. Corrections live in the database and merge by frame at render time, never in the artifact, which is rewritten wholesale by every re-analysis.

markerSaveRequest.title: MarkerSaveRequest
markerSaveRequest.description: A batch, deliberately not idempotent-per-click: a drag emits a position per pointer move and there is nothing to be gained from a request each.

stageMark.title: StageMark
stageMark.description: A hand-corrected swing stage: which frame this swing's `top` (or `impact`, …) really is.

stageSetRequest.title: StageSetRequest
stageSetRequest.description: One stage per request, unlike the marker batch: picking a stage is a single deliberate choice. `frame: null` clears it.

job.title: Job
job.description: One analyzer run over one clip. A swing with two cameras is two jobs, not one job that quietly does half the work. Job state lives in Postgres, not in a process.

runner.description: Which path runs the job: a child process of the web server (spawn) or the QStash-dispatched hosted worker (queue). Optional and informational — clients render progress identically either way.

jobStatusResponse.title: JobStatusResponse
jobStatusResponse.description: Either the job row, or `{ status: 'idle' }` when no run has ever been started for this view.

accountDeletion.title: AccountDeletion
accountDeletion.description: What DELETE /api/v1/account actually removed. Reported back rather than answered with 204 because a golfer deleting their account is entitled to see the count, and because a partial deletion has to be distinguishable from a complete one — three systems are involved and no transaction spans them.

userId.description: The account that was deleted. Always the caller — this route cannot name another.

mediaObjects.description: Objects removed across the source and artifact buckets.

views.description: Camera angles removed. A two-camera swing is two views.

authIdentityDeleted.description: False only where Supabase is unconfigured (the local development split, D7). The row data is gone either way; a client must not claim a full deletion when this is false.

swingDeletion.title: SwingDeletion
swingDeletion.description: What DELETE /api/v1/swings/:id removed. Reported rather than answered with 204 for the same reason accountDeletion is: media objects and database rows are two systems with no transaction spanning them, so a partial deletion must be distinguishable from a complete one.

swingId.description: The swing that was deleted. Always one the caller owns — the route answers 404 rather than touch another account's swing.

mediaObjects.description: Objects removed across the source and artifact buckets for this swing.
